text:
sara: Heads-up — intermittent packet loss on VXLAN/Geneve inside us-west2b GPU clusters starting ~09:10 UTC. Seeing grpc retries during large model downloads and a spike in application-level retransmits.

devin: saw 502s from beamline jobs too, coincides with autoscaler up events. any pattern on node type or AZ?

sara: mostly p4d pools and a couple of p3dn hosts. Spread across two k8s nodepools, not all pods in a single AZ.

leo: can you dump a quick tcpdump or netstat from one affected node? also check dmesg for mlx warnings.

sara: attaching quick snips:
```
# tcpdump -n -s 128 -c 50 -w /tmp/snap.pcap 'ip and vxlan'
reading 50 packets
50 packets captured
# ethtool -k eth0
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
scaling: on
ntuple-filters: off
# ip link show dev vxlan0
5: vxlan0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN
```

anita: mtu 1450 is odd — should be 9000 across GPU pools. could be a misconfigured CNI or calico route rewriting.

devin: confirmed nodes in that pool had MTU forced to 1450 after a kube-proxy/eni change last week, rolling update might have missed some.

kai: also check offloads: we've seen GSO/GRO interactions with vxlan and some mlx5 firmware causing fragmented user-visible drops. try toggling gso/gro off on vxlan interface to see if it stabilizes.

sara: tried `ethtool -K vxlan0 gso off gro off` on one node — immediate drop in retransmits for pods on that host, but throughput degraded.

leo: useful signal. that points to LSO/GSO edge-case. can we capture kernel logs around the times of packet drops? `dmesg --ctime | tail -n 200` might show firmware msgs.

sara: dmesg shows occasional "mlx5_core: CQE error" around the periods.

anita: qa: is RDMA enabled on these instances? p4d might use mlx5 and RDMA. if RDMA paths degrade, the overlay might fallback or drop fragments.

kai: yes RDMA stack present. this looks similar to earlier offload regressions. propose: 1) place an emergency canary with GSO/GRO off on a subset, 2) bump MTU to 9000 if the node's host ENI supports it, 3) collect per-packet NIC counters and firmware logs and open ticket with nic vendor.

devin: agree. also add a temporary routing policy to prefer the non-overlay path for large downloads until we have a fix (sticky annotation on pods).

sara: spinning a canary job with offloads disabled and higher MTU on 3 nodes now. will report perf and error rates.

ops-bot: deploy started: canary/overlay-offload-test -> 3 nodes (p4d-usw2b-*) by sara at 2025-03-20T09:45:11Z :hourglass_flowing_sand:

leo: if canary looks good, schedule a controlled roll where we toggle one host at a time. track tails in tsdb for packet_drops and grpc_latencies.

anita: logging next steps: collect `ethtool -S eth0` counters hourly and upload to s3 path `s3://redwood-telemetry/overlay-offload/175934/` so vendor can consume.

sara: update: after 20m with offloads off, grpc error rate dropped ~80% on canary. throughput down ~10% but acceptable. rolling to 6 more nodes.

kai: good. open vendor support ticket with captures + ethtool -S + dmesg. include NIC firmware and kernel versions.

devin: also flag Dedicated customers using that pool — elevated support watch. I posted a short status note in #customer-impact.

sara: will keep thread updated. thanks all. :thumbsup:
